summary: A 'kill' fault targeting the 'things' service resulted in a significant reduction in p95 latency for both direct and search operations, with zero errors and no data loss recorded.

root_cause_hypotheses.hypothesis: The targeted 'things' service instance was likely a degraded or 'poison' node whose removal allowed the load balancer to route traffic to more performant instances.
root_cause_hypotheses.supporting_evidence: Direct p95 latency decreased by 44.4% (-40.6ms) and search p95 latency decreased by 60.1% (-82.3ms) during the fault.

findings.recommended_fix: Investigate automated health checks and outlier detection to proactively remove or restart degraded service instances that negatively impact tail latency.
findings.title: Significant Latency Improvement During Service Outage
findings.impact: The system performed significantly better with one fewer instance, suggesting the baseline state included an underperforming node.

findings.recommended_fix: None required for availability; current redundancy levels are effective.
findings.title: High Availability and Fault Tolerance
findings.impact: The 'things' service demonstrated perfect availability and data integrity during a node failure.

recommended_next_experiment: Perform a 'kill' fault on a different instance of the 'things' service to determine if the latency improvement is reproducible or specific to the node targeted in this experiment.
